title: Effect of High-Dose Omega-3 Fatty Acids vs Corn Oil on Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Patients at High Cardiovascular Risk: The STRENGTH Randomized Clinical Trial
authors: Nicholls SJ, Lincoff AM, Garcia M, Bash D, Ballantyne CM, Barter PJ, et al.
followUp: median 42.0 months; stopped early for futility
population: Statin-treated adults at high cardiovascular risk with triglycerides 180 to below 500 mg/dl and HDL cholesterol below 42 mg/dl (men) or 47 mg/dl (women); 675 hospitals in 22 countries; 70% with diabetes
funder: The trial was funded by AstraZeneca AB and coordinated by the Cleveland Clinic Coordinating Center for Clinical Research (C5Research). The sponsor participated actively in designing the study in collaboration with the steering committee, provided logistical support and maintained the trial database; statistical analyses were performed at C5Research by an independent statistician on a copy of the database; the sponsor was permitted to review the manuscript and make suggestions, and final decisions on content were retained by the academic authors.
authorConflicts: Six authors were affiliated with AstraZeneca; Davidson founded Omthera Pharmaceuticals, which developed the study drug (Epanova) and was acquired by AstraZeneca in 2013, and was an AstraZeneca employee from 2013 to 2015; several academic authors reported grants or fees from AstraZeneca during the study, and Ridker reported grants from Amarin.
result: Omega-3 carboxylic acids (EPA and DHA) 4 g/day versus corn oil, 6539 per group. Primary composite (cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary revascularisation or hospitalisation for unstable angina) 785 (12.0%) versus 795 (12.2%) (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.09); cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke 541 (8.3%) versus 517 (7.9%) (HR 1.05, 0.93 to 1.19); death from any cause 373 (5.7%) versus 333 (5.1%). New-onset atrial fibrillation 2.2% versus 1.3% (HR 1.69, 1.29 to 2.21), number needed to harm 114; gastrointestinal adverse events 24.7% versus 14.7%. Triglycerides -19.0% versus -0.9%, hs-CRP -20.0% versus -6.3%, LDL cholesterol +1.2% versus -1.1%. The authors cite concerns over a greater than 30% increase in CRP in the mineral-oil group of REDUCE-IT, report that adverse effects on apolipoprotein B, LDL cholesterol and hs-CRP seen with mineral oil were not observed with corn oil, and state that these effects may have contributed to the apparent benefit of icosapent ethyl.
